claim: Many ensemble-based offline RL algorithms compute each Q-network's Bellman target using a SHARED pessimistic value (e.g., the min or mean-minus-std across the whole ensemble) rather than each member's own independently bootstrapped target -- and this shared-target design can paradoxically make the resulting Q-estimates effectively optimistic rather than pessimistic.
stance_target: the assumption that using a pessimistic aggregation function (e.g. min, LCB) over an ensemble automatically yields a pessimistic/conservative value estimate
scope_conditions: ensemble-of-Q-functions offline RL algorithms with shared Bellman targets
quoted_support: we demonstrate that using shared pessimistic targets can paradoxically lead to Q-estimates which are in fact optimistic! We verify our finding by constructing pedagogical toy MDPs. These results demonstrate that the formulation of using shared pessimistic targets is fundamentally ill-formed.

claim: Training each ensemble member's target network completely independently (no shared targets), then aggregating via mean-minus-standard-deviation (MSG algorithm), restores genuine pessimism and matches or significantly exceeds prior SOTA on challenging D4RL antmaze tasks and RL Unplugged.
stance_target: fix for the shared-target pessimism-inversion flaw
scope_conditions: D4RL antmaze domains, RL Unplugged benchmark
quoted_support: Crucially, ensembles trained with independent target values will always provide pessimistic value estimates. The pessimistic lower-confidence bound (LCB) value estimate ... is then used to update the policy being trained ... MSG matches, and in the more challenging domains such as antmazes, significantly exceeds the prior state-of-the-art.

claim: The paper's ablations isolate ensemble target-independence (not merely ensemble size) as the load-bearing factor for whether an ensemble-based pessimism mechanism actually behaves conservatively.
stance_target: precedent for attributing an ensemble-based method's safety/pessimism behavior to a specific implementation-level mechanism rather than to ensembling per se
quoted_support: through a series of ablation experiments on benchmark domains, we verify the significance of our theoretical findings, study the role of ensemble size, and highlight the settings in which ensembles provide the most benefit.

claim: The paper's own theoretical/empirical scope is entirely within ONE surrogate model class (ensembles of Q-networks); it studies an internal training-procedure axis (shared vs. independent target computation, and full deep ensembles vs. weight-sharing 'efficient ensemble' approximations) and never compares across genuinely distinct surrogate families such as a GP versus a neural ensemble.
stance_target: The audited paper's characterization of Ghasemipour et al. 2022 as the 'offline-RL instance' of a claim about fixed multipliers being incomparable ACROSS MODEL CLASSES
scope_conditions: full-text review of the ~22,000-word arXiv/ar5iv body
quoted_support: In this section we identify a critical flaw in how ensembles are commonly employed -- in offline as well as online RL -- for obtaining pessimistic value estimates ... Pessimistic Q-Ensembles: Independent or Shared Targets?

claim: 'Efficient ensemble' approximations (MIMO, Batch Ensembles, Multi-Head weight-sharing architectures) from the supervised-learning literature are very unreliable in challenging offline RL domains (D4RL antmaze) compared to full deep ensembles with separate independently-initialized networks, and fail for most hyperparameter choices.
stance_target: When ensemble uncertainty estimation is reliable versus not, as a function of ensemble construction/diversification
scope_conditions: D4RL antmaze domains, ensemble sizes N=4 and N=64
quoted_support: As can be seen, compared to MSG with deep ensembles (separate networks), the efficient ensemble approaches we consider are very unreliable, and fail for most hyperparameter choices.

claim: Full deep ensembles (same architecture, same data/objective, differing only by random weight initialization -- i.e. the standard Lakshminarayanan-style MSE-trained construction) are treated in this paper's own framing as the reliable, state-of-the-art choice for uncertainty estimation, citing Ovadia et al. 2019 for calibrated confidence bounds; it is the efficient/weight-sharing approximations of that construction which underperform, not the MSE-trained deep-ensemble construction itself.
stance_target: Any general claim that MSE-trained empirical-variance deep ensembles are unreliable uncertainty estimators as a class
scope_conditions: supervised-learning uncertainty estimation literature as characterized by this paper's related work; offline RL Q-ensembles specifically
quoted_support: In the deep learning literature, deep ensembles refers to the setting where the same network architectures are trained using the same data and objective functions, with the only difference in ensemble members being the random weight initialization of the networks... ensembles are state-of-the-art for accuracy and calibration (Ovadia et al., 2019).

claim: When the offline dataset only contains a narrow data distribution (e.g. imitation-learning-like data with low diversity), ensembles cannot make accurate predictions for unseen state-action pairs and require an additional support-constraint regularizer to compensate -- i.e. ensemble-variance informativeness depends on data coverage/diversity, not solely on the ensemble mechanism.
stance_target: A structural link between data coverage/distance-from-training-data and whether ensemble uncertainty is informative (adjacent to, but not identical with, a 'sigma is a distance signal' claim)
scope_conditions: D4RL Gym domains with narrow/imitation-learning-like offline datasets
quoted_support: We believe this is because the power of ensembles comes from predicting a value distribution for unseen (s,a) based on the available training data. Thus, if no data for sub-optimal actions is present, ensembles cannot make accurate predictions.

claim: Larger ensemble size (4 to 64 members) yields no noticeable performance gain on D4RL Gym tasks with low data diversity, but yields a clear upward trend on the harder, more data-diverse antmaze-large tasks.
stance_target: Ensemble-size sensitivity as a function of task/data diversity
scope_conditions: D4RL Gym and antmaze domains, ensemble sizes {1,4,16,64}
quoted_support: In domains such as D4RL Gym where offline datasets are qualitatively similar to imitation learning datasets, larger ensembles do not result in noticeable gains. In domains such as D4RL antmaze which contain more data diversity, larger ensembles significantly improve the performance of agents.

claim: The bib entry cites this work as NeurIPS 2022, matching the actual publication venue (arXiv submitted May 2022, accepted NeurIPS 2022); no citation-year trap exists for ghasemipour2022pessimistic.
